description: This is a team of passionate innovators, problem-solvers, and technology enthusiasts driven by curiosity and a shared ambition to push beyond boundaries. Inspired by the immense energy of a hypernova, we aim to turn bold ideas into impactful solutions through creativity, collaboration, and engineering. We believe every great mission begins with a vision, and we're here to transform that vision into reality.
summary: MOONWATCH is a browser game that teaches kids aged 9 to 14 how space weather affects astronauts. The player is the Commander of a small lunar outpost. Each Sol (mission day), the player reads a forecast, shares limited power between solar panels, shield, and oxygen, then presses Next Sol to see what happens. Solar flares and coronal mass ejections in the game come from real NASA DONKI data. Every real event carries a "Real NASA event" badge with a short science fact. If the crew fails, a Debrief screen explains the cause chain step by step, so players learn why it happened and try again. A big 10-second choice at the Sol 214 scene tests quick thinking. The game has an HD-2D look, works offline with saved NASA snapshots, and collects no personal data.
details:
What it does

MOONWATCH puts the player in charge of a lunar outpost with a crew of four: Engineer, Doctor, Botanist, and Pilot. Each Sol, the player reads a forecast, then chooses whether solar panels are out, whether the shield is on, and the oxygen level. After pressing Next Sol, the game works out power, oxygen, shield, and crew health. The player wins by surviving all Sols and loses if oxygen or crew health reaches zero. A Debrief screen shows the cause chain, for example: flare hit, panels left out, battery drained, oxygen systems off, crew health fell.

Real NASA data

Solar flare and coronal mass ejection events come from NASA's DONKI database. A server function fetches them with a hidden API key and turns them into game events. Real events show a "Real NASA event" badge, the date, and a one-line fact. Saved snapshots of real events keep the game working offline.

Benefits and impact

Kids learn cause and effect in space operations by making choices and seeing results. A run takes 3 to 8 minutes, needs no sign-up, and collects no personal data, so it suits classrooms.

Tools used

React, Vite, React Three Fiber (three.js), Zustand, Howler.js, Supabase (database), Vercel (hosting and serverless functions), Vitest and ESLint for testing and code quality.

Creativity

HD-2D style, inspired by Octopath Traveler: pixel-art crew inside a lit 3D diorama. The lighting changes with day, night, flares, and dust storms. Crew members show worry, run to shelter, and cheer.

Factors we considered

Child safety and privacy, accessibility (keyboard play, colour-blind safe gauges, reduced motion), offline reliability, fair difficulty, and free-licensed assets with credits.
